adapter_scope.found_by: reviewing this round change before handing it back: the first version of the guard read the identity file and did not check the adapter, which would have been a cross-adapter regression
adapter_scope.regression: packages/bridge-server/tests/host-spawner.test.ts pins both other adapters as not-applicable
adapter_scope.rule: the spawner question is asked only for the adapter whose launch command carries the conversation on --session-id
adapter_scope.why: every adapter writes host-identity.json, so gating on that file alone would make this guard refuse Codex (identity in CODEX_THREAD_ID) and OpenCode (identity in a per-call _meta field) on every call - their host process command lines carry no --session-id at all

deliberate_refusals: A surface that runs many conversations in one long-lived process (dsh web) puts no --session-id on that process, so the question cannot be answered there and calls are refused rather than allowed. That is the agreed choice for this adapter: proceeding unproven is the defect.
An operator can set TSUNAGOU_TRUST_UNPROVEN_HOST=1 to restore the previous behaviour. Doing so reopens the counterexample and must be recorded as such wherever it is used.
mechanism: a Harness conversation that is being driven was started with --session-id <its conversation>; a child can read its parent process command line, so the bridge compares that value with the conversation_id recorded in its own host-identity.json.
not_yet_done: the deepseek adapter documentation and the host matrix still describe the overlay alone as the binding
the adapter scoping is pinned by unit tests; the deepseek enforcement is verified end to end on the real host both before and after that change

what_changed: packages/bridge-server/src/host-spawner.ts now asks whether the process that spawned this bridge was started for the conversation this bridge is enrolled for, and packages/bridge-server/src/server.ts refuses a tool call before anything reaches the daemon when that question cannot be answered or answers no.
why_configuration_could_not_do_it: mcp-call-context.json: tools/call carries name plus arguments only, the child environment is scrubbedParentEnv() plus the copyable entry config, so an entry carries a credential and not a proof of the caller.
withdrawn: HISTORICAL: this records a guard that has since been DELETED. It was bypassable - the third review put '--session-id <enrolled id>' inside an ordinary prompt argument and the guard let the new conversation through - and it also refused the helper agent connect uses, breaking enrollment. packages/bridge-server/src/server.ts is back at its committed state and no code refuses an unproven caller. Kept as the record of an attempt, not as current behaviour.
